# Musk drops fraud claims against OpenAI, Altman ahead of trial

![Elon Musk delivers a speech during the World Economic Forum Annual Meeting in Davos, Switzerland, on January 22, 2026. ](https://fortune.com/img-assets/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/GettyImages-2256975324-e1777151790299.jpg?format=webp&w=1440&q=100)

Elon Musk delivers a speech during the World Economic Forum Annual Meeting in Davos, Switzerland, on January 22, 2026. Harun Ozalp/Anadolu via Getty Images

Elon Musk dropped his fraud claims against OpenAI and co-founders Sam Altman and Greg Brockman, narrowing the scope of his lawsuit against his business rivals on the eve of trial.

Recommended Video

* * *

US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers on Friday agreed to Musk’s request to “streamline” the case, leaving just two claims to proceed to trial of the 26 included in his November [2024 complaint](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-11-15/musk-escalates-altman-legal-feud-casting-openai-as-monopolist).

Jury selection is set for Monday in federal court in Oakland, California. Musk alleges the artificial intelligence startup abandoned its founding mission as a nonprofit to benefit humanity when it took billions of dollars in backing from [Microsoft](https://fortune.com/company/microsoft/) Corp. and planned its restructuring as a for-profit business.

Musk is seeking as much as $134 billion in damages that he has asked be directed to OpenAI’s charitable arm, if he wins at trial. He also wants a court order restoring the firm’s status as a nonprofit research organization and wants a judge to order that Altman and Brockman both be removed from their roles at OpenAI. Altman is chief executive officer and Brockman serves as president.

Read More: [OpenAI Accuses Musk of ‘Ambush’ as $100 Billion-Plus Trial Looms](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-04-11/openai-accuses-musk-of-ambush-as-100-billion-plus-trial-looms)

OpenAI complained to the judge two weeks ago that the remedies proposed by Musk were an 11th-hour surprise and accused the world’s richest person of a “legal ambush” with the trial looming.

OpenAI, Altman, Brockman and Microsoft have all denied wrongdoing, saying Musk’s claims are baseless harassment.

The trial will be divided into two phases. During the first portion, a jury will hear arguments and testimony about Musk’s allegations, which now focus on two claims — unjust enrichment and breach of charitable trust.

The panel will issue an “advisory verdict” that will not be binding on Gonzalez Rogers, who will ultimately decide whether Musk proved his claims.

In the second part of the proceedings, Gonzalez Rogers will hear arguments on the remedies Musk is seeking and issue a ruling.

Musk co-founded OpenAI with Altman and others in 2015, but the former business partners have become bitter foes in recent years. Musk left OpenAI’s board in 2018 and in 2023 co-founded the artificial intelligence company xAI, which has become one of OpenAI’s main rivals.

Last February, OpenAI rejected Musk’s unsolicited bid to acquire the assets of the nonprofit that controls the company for $97.4 billion. Months later, the company completed its for-profit restructuring plan, paving the way for it to raise more capital and potentially go public.

The case is Musk v. Altman, 4:24-cv-04722, US District Court, Northern District of California (Oakland).

](https://enterpriseai.economictimes.indiatimes.com/images/default.jpg)Elon MuskNew Delhi: Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla, has reportedly withdrawn fraud claims against OpenAI and its co-founders [Sam Altman](https://enterpriseai.economictimes.indiatimes.com/tag/sam+altman) and [Greg Brockman](https://enterpriseai.economictimes.indiatimes.com/tag/greg+brockman), narrowing the scope of his lawsuit on the eve of trial. As per reports, Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers, a US court judge, has allowed Musk to streamline the case, leaving just two claims, unjust enrichment and breach of charitable trust, out of the 26 included in his Nov 2024 complaint. Jury selection is scheduled to begin on Monday in a federal court in Oakland, California. Musk has alleged that OpenAI deviated from its founding mission as a non-profit aimed at benefiting humanity after securing billions of dollars in funding from Microsoft and transitioning towards a for-profit structure. He is seeking damages of up to $134 billion, which he said should be directed to OpenAI’s charitable arm if he succeeds. Musk has also requested the court to restore the organisation’s nonprofit status and remove Altman and Brockman from their leadership roles. However, OpenAI, along with Altman, Brockman and Microsoft, has denied the allegations, calling them baseless and accusing Musk of introducing last-minute demands ahead of the trial. The trial will proceed in two phases. In the first phase, a jury will hear arguments related to the remaining claims and issue a non-binding advisory verdict. In the second phase, the judge will decide on the remedies sought by Musk. Musk co-founded OpenAI in 2015 but exited its Board in 2018. He later launched rival AI firm xAI in 2023, intensifying competition in the rapidly evolving Artificial Intelligence space. Earlier in April, Musk sought the removal of Altman and Brockman as part of his legal challenge to the Artificial Intelligence firm’s shift to a for-profit structure, according to reports. - [TNN & Agencies](https://enterpriseai.economictimes.indiatimes.com/agency/87654320/TNN-&-Agencies) - Published On Apr 26, 2026 at 04:35 PM IST - - Telegram - Facebook - Copy Link ## Comments ![comment](https://st.etb2bimg.com/Themes/Release/theme4/images/et-default-user_1.svg) What are your thoughts? ### Musk narrows lawsuit against Sam Altman two days before trial

### Only two of 26 claims remain: unjust enrichment and charitable-trust violations

![Photo: Shutterstock](https://media.bloomingbit.io/news/dc1cea7f-a0ba-4105-80f1-8088843b7ed9.webp?w=800)_Photo: Shutterstock_

Elon Musk, Tesla’s chief executive officer, has withdrawn most of his claims against OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman two days before a major court fight is set to begin. Musk has also said that if he wins, he would place OpenAI under a charitable foundation.

Bloomberg and Reuters reported on April 25 that Musk would drop all but two of his 26 claims, leaving only unjust enrichment and charitable-trust violations. Musk has long argued that Altman misled him by promising to develop open-source artificial intelligence for the benefit of humanity to counter Google’s DeepMind.

Musk has repeatedly called Altman a “swindler” on social media. He also withdrew fraud-related claims he had brought against Altman and OpenAI President Greg Brockman.

Musk argues that OpenAI was founded as a nonprofit but later turned into a for-profit company with backing from Microsoft. He says he contributed $38 million in seed funding in 2015, and that OpenAI then broke its nonprofit pledge and improperly profited from the shift.

Musk has said that if he prevails, he would place OpenAI under a charitable foundation. He is seeking damages of as much as $134 billion and said he would turn that amount over to an OpenAI charitable foundation if he wins.

He has also called for Altman and Brockman to be removed. Altman, Brockman and Microsoft have pushed back, calling Musk’s claims baseless harassment. Musk and Altman once worked together to lead OpenAI. Their relationship soured after Musk left the company in 2018.

The lawsuit between the two technology-industry heavyweights was filed in 2024. Formal proceedings are scheduled to begin on April 27. Juror selection is set for April 27 at federal district court in Oakland, California, with opening statements planned for April 28.

# Musk drops fraud claims in OpenAI lawsuit, two claims head to trial

Published: 25 April 2026


[Comments](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/musk-drops-fraud-claims-in-openai-lawsuit-two-claims-head-to-trial/#comments-reply "Comments")

- ![Anna Zhadan](https://media.cybernews.com/images/124w/2022/06/Anna-Zhadan.png)
[Anna Zhadan](https://cybernews.com/author/annaz/)


Contributor



* * *

![Elon Musk, Sam Altman, OpenAI](https://media.cybernews.com/images/featured-big/2024/06/MuskAltmanlawsuit.jpg)
Jonathan Ernst/Reuters \| Photosince/Shutterstock


**_Elon Musk dropped his fraud claims against OpenAI and its co-founders, but a US judge plans to proceed to trial on other claims._**

On April 24th, US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers agreed to dismiss Musk’s fraud and constructive fraud claims in a bid to streamline the case.

This would leave just two claims to proceed to trial of the 26 originally included in his November 2024 complaint, specifically, unjust enrichment and breach of charitable trust.

ADVERTISEMENT

According to Musk, this would allow jurors [to focus on his goal](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/artificial-intelligence/us-judge-dismisses-elon-musks-fraud-claims-in-openai-case-at-his-request-plans-to-proceed-to-trial/articleshow/130509943.cms?from=mdr) of ensuring that OpenAI benefits humanity rather than serving as a “wealth machine.”

Jury selection is scheduled to begin Monday, with opening arguments to follow on Tuesday.

![jurgita](data:image/svg+xml;charset%3D'utf-8',%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D'http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg'%20viewBox%3D'0%200%2032%2032'%2F%3E)![justinasv](data:image/svg+xml;charset%3D'utf-8',%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D'http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg'%20viewBox%3D'0%200%2032%2032'%2F%3E)![Izabelė Pukėnaitė](data:image/svg+xml;charset%3D'utf-8',%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D'http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg'%20viewBox%3D'0%200%2032%2032'%2F%3E)![vilius](data:image/svg+xml;charset%3D'utf-8',%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D'http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg'%20viewBox%3D'0%200%2032%2032'%2F%3E)![Ernestas Naprys](data:image/svg+xml;charset%3D'utf-8',%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D'http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg'%20viewBox%3D'0%200%2032%2032'%2F%3E)![Gintaras Radauskas](data:image/svg+xml;charset%3D'utf-8',%3Csvg%20xmlns%3D'http%3A%2F%2Fwww.w3.org%2F2000%2Fsvg'%20viewBox%3D'0%200%2032%2032'%2F%3E)

Don't miss our latest stories on Google News

[Google News\\
Follow us](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAqBwgKMLWJmAswvLOvAw?hl=en-US&gl=US&ceid=US%3Aen)

Musk is [seeking between $79 billion and $134 billion in damages](https://cybernews.com/news/musk-seeking-up-to-134bn-from-openai-microsoft-in-wrongful-gains/) from OpenAI and one of its largest investors, Microsoft, claiming that it abandoned its original plans of operating as a non-profit organization and misled both him and the public.

Musk, who co-founded OpenAI with CEO Sam Altman and others in 2015, left the board in 2018 and later co-founded one of its main rivals, xAI. Ever since, the relationship between the former co-founders has been rocky, with Musk publicly going after Altman on X: “You stole a non-profit.”

In addition to monetary damages, Musk is seeking a court order to restore the firm’s status as a non-profit research organisation and to remove Altman and OpenAI President Greg Brockman from their roles.

The company and its leaders have all denied wrongdoing, with OpenAI claiming that the lawsuit is “part of \[Musk’s\] ongoing pattern of harassment.” The company also said that Musk is trying to slow them down and benefit his own business, xAI.

Proceeds from any damages would go to OpenAI’s charitable arm, according to a person involved in the case.

In February last year, OpenAI [rejected a $97.4 billion bid from Musk](https://cybernews.com/ai-news/openai-board-rejects-musks-97-4-billion-offer/), saying: "OpenAI is not for sale.”

_Reuters_ reported that the company is preparing for an IPO that could value it at up to $1 trillion.

news.markdown:
#### Key Points

- U.S. District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers dismissed Elon Musk's fraud and constructive fraud claims against OpenAI and Sam Altman following Musk's motion[1](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source").
- The ruling streamlines the case, allowing trial to proceed on breach of charitable trust and unjust enrichment claims[1](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source").
- Jury selection begins Monday, with opening arguments scheduled for Tuesday[1](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source").
- Musk seeks to enforce OpenAI's original mission to benefit humanity, not profits, amid allegations involving Microsoft[3](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source").
- Musk is pursuing $150 billion in damages, with proceeds directed to OpenAI’s charitable arm[3](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source").

![US Court Dismisses Musk's Fraud Allegations Against OpenAI on His Request Ahead of Trial](https://mlq.ai/media/news_images/musk-openai-drop.png)

A U.S. federal judge in Oakland, California, on Friday dismissed Elon Musk's fraud claims in his lawsuit against OpenAI and co-founder Sam Altman at Musk's own request, narrowing the case ahead of trial. The court will proceed with Musk's remaining claims of breach of charitable trust and unjust enrichment, with jury selection set to start Monday[1](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source").

## Case Background

Elon Musk, a co-founder of OpenAI, filed the lawsuit accusing OpenAI and Sam Altman of betraying the organization's original mission to develop artificial intelligence for the benefit of humanity. Musk alleges that OpenAI shifted to a for-profit model in 2019 after he left the board, prioritizing profits over public good, with involvement from Microsoft, one of OpenAI's largest investors[1](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source"). The dismissal of fraud and constructive fraud claims was proposed by Musk to streamline proceedings and focus jurors on core issues[3](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source") [4](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source").


## Court Ruling Details

U.S. District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers issued the ruling on April 24, 2026, granting Musk's motion to drop the fraud allegations. This leaves breach of charitable trust and unjust enrichment as the key claims moving forward. Jury selection is scheduled for Monday, followed by opening arguments on Tuesday, setting the stage for a focused trial[1](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source").


## Musk's Objectives

Musk stated that dismissing the fraud claims would keep the trial centered on ensuring OpenAI benefits humanity rather than becoming a 'wealth machine.' He is seeking $150 billion in damages, according to a person involved in the case, with any proceeds going to OpenAI’s charitable arm[3](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source").


## Litigation Strategy Shift

The dismissal of fraud claims at Musk's request represents a strategic pivot in the litigation, sharpening the focus on OpenAI's governance and adherence to its founding charter as a nonprofit entity dedicated to public benefit. By eliminating potentially complex fraud arguments, Musk avoids diluting the jury's attention on what he views as the heart of the dispute: whether OpenAI's transition to a for-profit structure, backed by Microsoft, violates its charitable trust obligations. This move could strengthen Musk's position by presenting a clearer narrative of mission betrayal rather than getting mired in evidentiary hurdles around intent and misrepresentation[3](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source") [4](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source").

The remaining claims of breach of charitable trust and unjust enrichment carry significant weight in nonprofit law, potentially setting precedents for how AI organizations balance mission-driven origins with commercial pressures. OpenAI's defense will likely hinge on arguments that its capped-profit model aligns with long-term humanity benefits, while Microsoft's role as an investor underscores the tensions between tech philanthropy and market dynamics. This streamlining may expedite resolution but heightens scrutiny on OpenAI's internal structures and Altman's leadership[1](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source") [2](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source").


## Trial Timeline and Implications

With jury selection starting Monday and opening arguments on Tuesday, the trial is poised to unfold rapidly, potentially reaching a verdict within weeks depending on evidence presentation and witness testimonies. Musk's emphasis on charitable trust could influence jury perceptions, especially given public interest in AI ethics and corporate accountability, while OpenAI may counter with demonstrations of its ongoing humanitarian AI efforts[1](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source").

A ruling in Musk's favor could force OpenAI to restructure or redirect profits to charitable causes, impacting its competitive edge against rivals like xAI, Musk's own venture. Conversely, validation of OpenAI's model might encourage similar for-profit shifts in other AI nonprofits. Post-trial appeals remain likely, prolonging uncertainty, but the outcome will shape governance norms in the AI sector amid growing regulatory attention[2](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source") [3](https://mlq.ai/news/us-court-dismisses-musks-fraud-allegations-against-openai-on-his-request-ahead-of-trial/# "Click to view source").

Market reactions will closely follow, particularly for Microsoft as OpenAI's key partner, with potential implications for investment strategies in AI startups balancing profit and purpose.
